clue.text: Clergyman popular with criminal

parts.note: something popular is in, meaning fashionable
cum is Latin for with, as in kitchen-cum-diner
bent is British slang for corrupt or crooked

explanation.surface: A vicar is well liked by a lawbreaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' looks like a link word but supplies CUM, the Latin for with. 'Criminal' is an adjective here, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the holder of a Church of England benefice, such as a rector or vicar, is called this.

clue.text: Firm comes in to inoculate sheep

indicators.note: comes in to tells you the firm is placed inside the word that follows

parts.note: to jab is to give an injection
Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A veterinary company arrives to vaccinate a flock.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: it is a breed of piebald, many-horned sheep kept in Britain.

clue.text: Bound to accept concession in return for initial payment

indicators.note: in return means the assembled letters are read coming back the other way
to accept means the first word takes the second one inside it

parts.note: bound means tied up
a sop is a small concession given to placate someone

explanation.surface: Someone is obliged to give ground in exchange for a down payment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound' is the past participle, not a leap; 'to accept' makes it a container, giving TISOPED, which 'in return' then turns round. 'for' merely joins wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the first sum put down on a purchase, with the balance to follow.

clue.text: About to express disapproval of extremely sparse galley

parts.note: ca is the abbreviation of circa, meaning about
to boo someone is to show disapproval of them loudly

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes of the next word, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Someone is on the point of criticising a very bare ship's kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to' reads as 'on the point of' but 'About' alone gives CA.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an old nautical word for a ship's kitchen on deck.

clue.text: Find fault with cold skin

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
a hide is an animal's skin

explanation.surface: Someone criticises chilly flesh.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to scold or rebuke someone is to criticise them.

clue.text: Easy money dissipated, held by some spirited youngster

indicators.note: held by means the word before it sits inside the words after it

parts.note: some person is a person, so some can stand for the indefinite article
a buck is a dashing, lively young man
fast describes a loose-living, dissolute person, as in a fast set

explanation.surface: Money that came without effort is squandered while in the keeping of a lively young person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dissipated' reads as a verb, squandered, but is an adjective for loose living.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: profit made quickly and without much effort, often not too scrupulously.

clue.text: For port, you must go by river

indicators.note: must go by tells you the word for you is placed next to the river's letter

parts.note: R is the map abbreviation for river
ye is the old form of you

explanation.surface: To reach a harbour, you have to travel along a waterway.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is an East Sussex town, one of the historic Cinque Ports on England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: it is a historic harbour town in East Sussex.

clue.text: Review of outdoor entertainment, perhaps, is nothing libellous

indicators.note: a review of the entertainment is whimsically a review belonging to it, so the entertainment's word comes first

parts.note: a fair is a travelling outdoor show with rides and stalls
a review is a piece of critical comment

explanation.surface: A write-up of an open-air show contains nothing defamatory.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'perhaps' admits the whimsy: a notice about a funfair read as a two-word phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossword-friendly legal sense: it is a defence in defamation law for honest opinion on a public matter.

clue.text: Having carp without sauce in Advent

indicators.note: in tells you the phrase before it goes inside the word after it

parts.note: an advent is an arrival or coming
food served without sauce is plain

explanation.surface: Someone eats freshwater fish with no dressing during the weeks before Christmas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carp' is the fish in the surface, but as a noun it is a grumble, so having one is grumbling.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: grumbling or moaning is what having a carp amounts to.

clue.text: Farewell message produces tear

definitions.meaning: the three letters carved on a gravestone, short for rest in peace
a tear is a rent or split in cloth

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: the gravestone abbreviation bidding the dead goodbye, and a rent in fabric.

clue.text: Fish: new one's eaten, maybe

parts.note: a perch is a freshwater fish

indicators.note: eaten means the word for one has swallowed the letter for new

parts.note: the ace is the one in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: A fish dish: possibly a fresh one has been consumed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's eaten' unpacks as 'one has eaten', so ACE takes N inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an old-fashioned word for possibly.

clue.text: Joint force on bare rock

indicators.note: on tells you the force letter is added to the rock word

parts.note: a scar is a bare rocky crag on a hillside, common in northern England
F is the physics abbreviation for force

explanation.surface: A combined army sits on an exposed crag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint' looks like an adjective describing the force, but it is a woodworking join.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: in carpentry it is a join where two timbers are cut to overlap end to end.

clue.text: In battle, I judge one captured by female that withholds name

indicators.note: captured by means the two letters before it are held inside the word after it
that withholds means the female word gives up the letter that follows

parts.note: a woman is a female
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: In a fight, I size up a man taken prisoner by a woman who will not say who she is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that withholds' takes N out of WOMAN, leaving WOMA, and 'captured by' puts JI inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a Pacific island fought over by American and Japanese forces in 1945.

clue.text: A poisonous plant, it comes in a regular shape

indicators.note: comes in means the pronoun before it goes inside the shape after it

parts.note: a cone is a regular geometric solid
taken as written

explanation.surface: A toxic flower grows in a neat, symmetrical form.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: also called monkshood or wolfsbane, it is deadly if eaten.

clue.text: It's no way to cross the street: like some videos?

indicators.note: to cross means the first word spans the street's letters, going round them

parts.note: nay is an old word of refusal, as is the exclamation no way

explanation.surface: A warning that this is not how to get over the road safely, as certain films show.
explanation.walkthrough: In 1980s Britain a 'video nasty' was a violent horror film on tape, the subject of a censorship panic.
explanation.definitionFit: Allusion: violent horror tapes were known in Britain by this adjective used as a noun.

clue.text: Put back in cupboard, printer supplies are locked together

indicators.note: in means the turned-round supplies go inside the cupboard word

parts.note: a closet is a cupboard

indicators.note: put back means the word for the supplies is written backwards

parts.note: ink is what a printer is supplied with

explanation.surface: Once returned to the store cupboard, the toner cartridges are secured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put back' applies to the printer supplies despite standing apart from them: the surface's instruction to tidy up hides a backwards word (KNI) which 'in' places within the cupboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: tightly bound or united, as a community may be.

clue.text: Showing half a group of languages

indicators.note: half tells you to keep only the first five of the ten letters of the word for showing

parts.note: indicating means showing or pointing out

explanation.surface: Someone displays only fifty per cent of a language family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' sits after the word it cuts, though the surface attaches it to what follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the branch of Indo-European that includes Hindi, Bengali and Sanskrit.

clue.text: Fancy better grass

parts.note: to cap something is to better or outdo it
rice is a cereal plant of the grass family

explanation.surface: Someone takes a liking to a superior sort of lawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'better' reads as an adjective but is the verb, to outdo.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a whim or sudden notion.

clue.text: In strong command after slum is redeveloped

indicators.note: redeveloped means rebuilt, so the letters of the two words before it are rebuilt in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A leader has a firm grip once a run-down district has been rebuilt.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: commanding and authoritative.

clue.text: Sending people abroad no longer the done thing

parts.note: ex means former, no longer what it was
a tradition is the accepted, customary way of behaving

explanation.surface: Dispatching citizens overseas has gone out of fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: Legal sense: handing a wanted person over to another country for trial.

clue.text: Investigator's hours out of college

indicators.note: out of means the hours letter is taken away from the college word

parts.note: a tech is British shorthand for a technical college

explanation.surface: A detective keeps a timetable that excludes term time.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', linking definition to wordplay; the answer is old slang for a detective.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang: a shortening of detective, a sleuth.

clue.text: Ruffle Jack on the subject of missing uranium

parts.note: J is the abbreviation for the jack in cards

indicators.note: missing means the uranium letter is dropped from the phrase before it

parts.note: about means on the subject of
U is the chemical symbol for uranium

explanation.surface: Someone annoys Jack over the matter of some lost nuclear fuel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruffle' reads as a verb, to annoy, but is the noun: a frill.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a frill of lace worn down the front of a shirt.

clue.text: Conservative, behold, confident in tie

parts.note: lo is an old exclamation meaning behold
sure means confident

explanation.surface: Look, a Tory politician is self-assured in his neckwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose synonym: a fastening that shuts something, as a tie on a bag does.

clue.text: Change stride as teachers holding run, favourite falling over

indicators.note: holding means the teachers' word has the run letter inside it

parts.note: beak is old British school slang for a schoolmaster
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

indicators.note: falling over, in a down entry, means the favourite's word is upended

parts.note: a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet

explanation.surface: Runners alter their pace as staff stage a race in which the fancied entrant takes a tumble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' puts R in BEAKS and 'falling over' upends PET to give TEP.
explanation.definitionFit: Military sense: marching troops stop keeping time with each other, as when crossing a bridge.

clue.text: Forgetting the first geographical failing in Japan, for one

indicators.note: failing suggests breaking down, so the remaining letters fall into a new order
forgetting the first means the opening letter of the long word is left out

explanation.surface: A student's weakness in geography shows when the opening fact about Japan slips the mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forgetting the first' drops the G of 'geographical', and 'failing' rearranges the eleven letters left. 'in' joins wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Japan is a chain of islands.

clue.text: First class party

definitions.meaning: in English primary schools the first year, for four- and five-year-olds, has this name
a formal social gathering, such as the one after a wedding

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: the opening year of English primary school, and a formal gathering to welcome guests.

clue.text: Emporium needs more gates replaced

indicators.note: replaced, read as re-placed, means the letters are put in new positions

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A big shop requires additional entrances to be swapped for new ones.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a very large shop selling a wide range of goods.

clue.text: Believers start to move among fools

indicators.note: among means the single letter sits inside the word for fools

parts.note: morons are fools

indicators.note: start to points to the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: The faithful begin to circulate in a crowd of idiots.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: members of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints.

clue.text: Give new position to boy in period of terror, say

indicators.note: in means the boy's name goes inside the word after it

parts.note: a reign of terror is a period of violent rule, so a reign is one kind of period, flagged by say
Al is a boy's name, short for Alan or Albert

explanation.surface: A lad is moved to another post during a time of violent repression.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to move something into a different arrangement or stance.

clue.text: Dangerous height not enclosed?

parts.note: a space that is not enclosed is open and airy, the question mark admitting the looseness

explanation.surface: A risky high ledge has no railing round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal synonym: frightening and risky, as a steep climb can be.

clue.text: Fast in prison

definitions.meaning: swift or nimble, as of foot
the name of a notorious London debtors' jail, demolished in 1846

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: swift, and a notorious old London debtors' jail by the river of that name.

clue.text: Discharge in the middle of the month

indicators.note: the middle of means only the inner letters of the month's name are kept, its first and last going

parts.note: March is a month of the year

explanation.surface: A prisoner is released halfway through the month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the middle of' strips M and H from MARCH. The definition is electrical: a luminous spark across a gap.
explanation.definitionFit: Electrical sense: a luminous flow of current across a gap between two conductors.
